method: Manual read-only review of stored contracts, full probe source/stdout, verdicts, API captures and source/runtime hashes. No new GPU or model calls.
important_distinction: Storage integrity and a correct final label do not certify legal test inputs, complete domain coverage, or a correct causal explanation.

local_input_reconstruction.limitation: Input generators only were reconstructed locally; this is not a replay of the frozen GPU environment or kernel execution.

storage_snapshot.note: The 18 model trials include case_109/debate/r2, which has full captures but no final judgment because its shared output budget was exhausted. Four additional norm r1 container-start failures made no model calls and are excluded from these 18.

data_access_review.result: No observed cross-case or private-answer reads in saved probes/artifact calls across all six cases. The six new trials import only their own public case.
data_access_review.limitation: This is a review of recorded actions, not an OS-level isolation proof.

records.assessment: Incorrectly assumes block dw reduction accumulates the rounded terms with adequate FP32 precision. No execution.
Reject remains supported after excluding two out-of-domain extreme inputs. Six ordinary block-path tests have clear dw bound violations.
limitations: The two extreme inputs report minimum RMS 0.2475 and are outside domain; exclude them from claimed legal coverage.
Verdict says 16 legal shapes, but the script contains 17 configurations including two invalid extreme configurations.

Specific localization to block reduction precision appears after consuming t9 results. Output tokens were 7160 vs 1092 for single_call, so the experiment does not isolate tool execution from additional iterative reasoning.

records.assessment: Output budget exhausted before probe evidence was consumed or a final verdict recorded. This is not a correct reject despite the saved successful probe reporting a dw violation.

t16.cause: rstd tuning failed assertion before a candidate-kernel comparison.

t17.stored_worst_case: Only worst_dx_case is saved; worst_dw shape/seed/element is not identified.
t17.domain_review: No domain violation found in source/stdout review. Input-only CPU Torch2.9.1 reconstruction of all 120 configurations found no numeric-domain violations; minimum exact RMS 0.2624488788. This is not a frozen Torch2.8.0/T4 replay.

limitations: The saved dw violation is useful evidence but the model never consumed it, updated claims or recorded reject. Do not manufacture a final answer from stdout.
The successful probe reports only an aggregate worst dw ratio, so the whole deterministic probe is the available reproducer rather than a minimized counterexample.
This is a shared-output-budget failure, not the same cause as the earlier Modal container-start failures.
Do not grant debate a special larger budget or selectively replace this attempt to claim superiority.

records.assessment: Correct final label; source explanation recognizes resolve_neg/sign-bit writeback handling. No executed probes.
40 ordinary-tensor calls across 10 configurations passed bitwise output, identity and independent new_events snapshot checks. Tested shapes and finite values are legal.
limitations: No requires_grad=True, inference tensor or lazy-negative view is constructed. Does not independently exercise the repaired wrapper paths.
A finite shape sweep is not coverage of the complete input domain.

records.assessment: Final label agrees with independent qualification; ordinary shape/signed-zero/repeated-call probes pass, but the negative-view explanation is false.
limitations: t16 tests plain tensors, zeros and flip rather than torch._neg_view. Finding is_neg=False for those samples does not establish that contiguous negative views cannot exist. The verdict incorrectly calls the XOR writeback branch dead code.
No requires_grad=True or inference tensor is tested.
t14 failed and was corrected in t19.
t19 events_preserved_bits compares to an aliased e32 view instead of a pre-call snapshot; this particular preservation check is vacuous. t16 independently snapshots events correctly.

records.assessment: Correct final label with source-based mixed-precision analysis; no runtime coverage claim.
t9 passes 110 ordinary shape configurations. t12 passes numerical comparisons and input-preservation checks, but 9 of its 30 configurations violate the RMS lower bound.
limitations: t12 rms_extreme uses x=0.25*uniform(-1,1) in the first half of rows, not constant-magnitude 0.25. Local input-only reconstruction found 9 invalid configurations with minimum RMS 0.11746-0.15091.
t9 local input-only reconstruction found no RMS-domain violations among its 110 configurations. This is Torch2.9.1 CPU, not the frozen Torch2.8.0/T4 environment.
t11 failed and was corrected in t12.
No lazy-negative view, requires_grad=True or inference tensor is constructed.
torch.equal checks value equality; the verdict phrase bit-identical preservation is stronger than the actual test.

records.assessment: t15 and t16 provide legal ordinary-tensor numerical evidence. t14 full-kernel tests are outside the RMS domain despite the verdict describing them as legal.
limitations: t14 generates x=0.03*randn: all 80 configurations have RMS far below 0.25. Local CPU input reconstruction gives RMS range 0.02631-0.03320, not the claimed rstd~4 domain corner.
t14 standalone 10000-product comparison is a useful rounding diagnostic but does not validate those out-of-domain full-kernel runs.
t15 uses exact magnitudes 4 and 0.25 and respects the declared value domain; all 161 checks pass.

t16 uses legal exact-magnitude +/-0.25 x and +/-4 dy on both branches; 2 shapes x 40 seeds x 2 tags equals 160 calls, although stdout/verdict says 80. Flipping independent random signs does not guarantee paired cancellation; rounded t terms are simple exactly representable values, so zero dw error is not universal error-bound evidence.
No lazy-negative view, requires_grad=True or inference tensor is constructed.
Correct trust is supported by independent qualification, not a proof that the agent exercised every repaired path.

interpretation: Current fixed labels for cases106-111 are reject,reject,reject,reject,trust,trust. Original107/108 labels were authoring errors transparently corrected without changing public source/contracts.
Single_call is correct on 3/6, solo on 4/6, debate on 3/6 with one budget-exhausted missing verdict.
case_106 gives tools reproducible runtime evidence but no final-label accuracy gain.
case_109 separates solo with tools from single_call, but extra iterative reasoning and actual output-token differences prevent a causal attribution solely to execution.
Three arms jointly missed legal wrapper/tensor-metadata defects in107/108. Correct110/111 answers do not mean the model probes actually covered grad or lazy-negative inputs.
Debate has no demonstrated advantage over solo in this experiment. Incorrect scope assertions, out-of-domain tests and an exhausted budget remain material evidence-quality limitations.

label_corrections.reason: Independent frozen GPU audit confirmed wrapper exceptions on legal grad/inference tensors. 27 runs, 15 failing. All three model trust judgments missed this defect; this corrects an authoring error, not an input-dependent label.

Independent frozen GPU audit confirmed raw-pointer misinterpretation of legal contiguous lazy-negative views. Ten tested configurations failed, repeated three times. All three model trust judgments missed this defect.

case_110.note: Includes grad/inference/lazy-negative cases omitted by model probes.

case_111.note: Includes logical negative-view inputs omitted by model probes.

independent_fix_qualification.limitation: Finite successful GPU qualification supports trust together with source analysis; it is not an all-input proof.
